precepts.text: I am the God of all flesh: pressed with it, the trinitarian answered that Christ is God over his own flesh, and his own side laughed.
precepts.point: There is no scripture that says the Father becomes his God when he is human as opposed to being his God always; that is pure theology, and it is the question that stumps them.

note.label: Untruthful Trinity Revisited & Ridiculous

precepts.why:
“I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother’s belly.” The trinitarians read it this way: when Christ came into the world as a human being, that's when his Father became his God. The Father has divine essence, the Holy Spirit has divine essence, the Son has divine essence, so when Christ came on the earth keeping humanity and godhood, he is his own god. And not only that: he is his own god and he has a God above him. That's two. It's a ridiculous argument.

“Behold, I am the Lord, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?” The Father is the God of all flesh. So if Christ is the essence of his Father, then Christ becomes the God of his own humanity, God over his own flesh. It's madness. Pressed with it in the debate, the trinitarian answered exactly that: Christ is God over his own flesh. And his own side laughed at him; you could see his friend's face in the back. They know that's stupid.

That one question stumped them. There is no scripture that says the heavenly Father becomes his God when he is human, as opposed to being his God always. That's pure theology. Ask them where the Bible says it. Nowhere in Psalms 22 do we read that Christ, out of his mother's womb, is fully God and fully man. That is a Greco-Roman hermeneutical interpretation; they even admitted there is an element of philosophy in it. It isn't an element; it's full-blown philosophy.

The scripture is clear. Resurrected and glorified, Christ says “my God” four times in one verse: “Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God.” And risen from the dead, “I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.” Even “being in the form of God”, he “thought it not robbery to be equal with God”, but “made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant”: God or man, he knew the Father was above him. These men follow the Greeks, “Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all”. They are unreasonable people, going in circles like a cartwheel, and you cannot waste your time with them.

precepts.text: Jeremiah, shut up in prison, warned Zedekiah he would not escape but be delivered to Babylon, see the king face to face, and not prosper in fighting the Chaldeans.
precepts.point: Through the anger of the Lord it came to pass in Jerusalem and Judah, until he had cast them out of his presence, that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

note.label: 2 Kings 24: Judah Carried Away for the Sins of Manasseh

precepts.why:
In “the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah”, when “the king of Babylon’s army besieged Jerusalem”, Jeremiah was “shut up in the court of the prison”. Zedekiah had shut him up for prophesying that the Lord would give the city into the hand of the king of Babylon.

Jeremiah warned him plainly: “Zedekiah king of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon, and shall speak with him mouth to mouth, and his eyes shall behold his eyes”. He would be led to Babylon, “and there shall he be until I visit him, saith the Lord: though ye fight with the Chaldeans, ye shall not prosper.”

That is the Zedekiah of this passage. The king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s father’s brother, king in his stead and changed his name to Zedekiah. He reigned eleven years and “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, according to all that Jehoiakim had done.” And “through the anger of the Lord” it came to pass that Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon, until the Lord had cast Judah out from his presence. He was warned, he rebelled anyway, and he could not prosper against the Chaldeans.

precepts.text: We are supposed to put all things in writing, for evidence is the only way to prove something.
precepts.point: Anathoth was in the country of Benjamin because the priests were given cities and suburbs to dwell in.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
Jeremiah did not just hand over the money for the field. He weighed him seventeen shekels of silver in the balances, subscribed the evidence, sealed it, took witnesses, and kept both the sealed evidence and the open according to the law and custom, then delivered it to Baruch the son of Neriah before all the Jews in the court of the prison.

That is the law: “Deliver all things in number and weight; and put all in writing that thou givest out, or receivest in.” We are supposed to put all things in writing. Evidence is the only way to prove something, and Jeremiah's purchase of the field in Anathoth, in the country of Benjamin where the priests were given cities and suburbs to dwell in, was done in number and weight and in writing.

precepts.text: The whole land would be a desolation and these nations serve the king of Babylon seventy years before He punished Babylon; after Babylon we passed to the Persians and Medes, and Cyrus the Persian let us return.
precepts.point: The Most High declares that houses, fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land, because the prophecy was that the captivity would last seventy years and then the people would return.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
Jeremiah had the evidences put in an earthen vessel “that they may continue many days”, because “Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.” The evidence had to last because the prophecy was that the captivity would last seventy years and then the people would return.

The Lord had already given the number: “And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.” The whole land would be a desolation and these nations serve the king of Babylon seventy years before he punished Babylon. After Babylon we passed to the Persians and Medes, and Cyrus the Persian let us return. Then the fields were possessed again, and the sealed and open evidence in the earthen vessel proved whose they were.

precepts.text: The curses came because we came in and possessed the land but would not walk in the ways of the Most High as He commanded.
precepts.point: The people came in and possessed the land but obeyed not His voice nor walked in His law, therefore He caused all this evil to come upon them, even as the mounts came up against the city to take it.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
In his prayer Jeremiah confesses the whole matter: the Lord gave our fathers the land flowing with milk and honey, “And they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do: therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them”.

That evil was the curse Moses had written: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. The curses came because we came in and possessed the land but would not walk in the ways of the Most High as he commanded. The mounts against the city, the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and the city given into the hand of the Chaldeans, are those curses overtaking us.

precepts.text: We were not to bring the abomination into our house, and definitely not into the house of the Most High to pollute it.
precepts.point: They built the high places of Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom to cause their sons and daughters to pass through the fire unto Molech, an abomination He never commanded.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
The people had offered incense to Baal on their roofs, set their abominations in the house called by the Lord's name to defile it, and built the high places of Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom to pass their children through the fire to Molech. The law had told us what to do with the gods of the nations: “The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: thou shalt not desire the silver or gold that is on them, nor take it unto thee, lest thou be snared therein: for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God.”

We were not to bring the abomination into our house, and definitely not into the house of the Most High to pollute it. Instead of burning the images with fire, Israel and Judah were snared by them. So the Chaldeans come and set fire on the city and burn it with the houses, on the same roofs where they offered incense to Baal: what they would not burn, he has this people's houses burned to the ground for.

precepts.text: There are no multiple ways and no multiple truths; there is one way to the Father through the Son, which answers why Christianity has so many denominations.
precepts.point: This is being seen today as we rise up and get understanding of who we are, our nationality, and our God being a black God for His people, a God who does not love all nations alike but will reward these nations for what they have done to us.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
When the Lord gathers Israel out of all countries where he drove them, “I will give them one heart, and one way, that they may fear me for ever”. One heart and one way means one mind and full agreement. Christ says what that one way is: “I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.”

There are no multiple ways and no multiple truths; there is one way to the Father, through the Son. That answers why Christianity has so many denominations: they are not walking in the one way. This is being seen today as we rise up and get understanding of who we are, our nationality, and our God being a black God for his people, a God who does not love all nations alike but will reward these nations for what they have done to us. He puts his fear in our hearts that we shall not depart from him, and plants us in the land with his whole heart and his whole soul.

precepts.text: All things are not yet fulfilled, for we are still scattered and cannot rightly keep the high holy days in our enemies' lands.
precepts.point: After the Babylonian and Persian captivities the northern kingdom came to the western hemisphere, so these things, us all being set back in the land and in full agreement, have yet to take place.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
The Lord promises fields bought again in Benjamin, about Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, the mountains, the valley and the south, “for I will cause their captivity to return”. After the Babylonian and Persian captivities the northern kingdom came to the western hemisphere, so these things, us all being set back in the land and in full agreement, have yet to take place.

Christ shows that the promises still stand: “Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled.” All things are not yet fulfilled, for we are still scattered and cannot rightly keep the high holy days in our enemies' lands. Not one jot or tittle of what the prophets spoke passes until it is done, so the good he promised will come as surely as the evil did.
